item.title: UN says workers' health 'severely impacted' by rising heat
item.description: Rising global temperatures are having an ever-worsening impact on the health and productivity of workers, the United Nations said Friday, urging immediate action to tackle the dangers of heat stress. "Immediate action is needed to address the worsening impact of heat stress on workers worldwide," they said.

item.title: Who is Sheikh Jassim, the Qatari billionaire who tried to buy Manchester United but failed?
item.description: Sheikh Jassim’s £4.79bn bid to fully acquire Manchester United in 2023 was rejected in favour of Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s 25% stake. Despite a new clause enabling full club sale, Jassim’s camp has ruled out returning, shifting focus to Qatar’s 2036 Olympic bid. The Qatari royal’s Nine Two Foundation is no longer pursuing European football club ownership.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sri Lanka's ex-president hospitalized: Wickremesinghe rushed to ICU; condition now 'stable'
item.description: Former Sri Lankan President Ranil Wickremesinghe, recently jailed and charged with misusing government funds, was admitted to the ICU due to severe dehydration and pre-existing conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure. His hospitalization followed his arrest as part of President Dissanayake's anti-corruption campaign. Opposition parties claim the charges are politically motivated, fearing Wickremesinghe's potential return to power.

item.title: Ramadan 2025: Saudi Arabia bans promotional activities during iftar at Islam’s holiest sites
item.description: Saudi Arabia has banned advertising during iftar meal distribution at Mecca's Grand Mosque and Medina's Prophet's Mosque to maintain sanctity during Ramadan. Only registered organizations with compliant plans can get permits, with violations leading to warnings or revocation. These guidelines aim to ensure order, respect, and public health, fostering devotion free from commercial distractions.

item.title: Kuwait inflation alert: Consumer prices rise 2.39% in July 2025 amid climbing costs of essentials
item.description: Kuwait witnessed a 2.39% surge in its consumer price index in July 2025, according to the Central Statistical Bureau. Escalating costs in food, healthcare, clothing, and education are primarily responsible, intensifying financial strain on households. While transportation costs decreased, food and beverages saw the highest increase at 5.63%. Excluding food, inflation still rose by 1.61%, indicating broad price pressures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Deadly extramarital affair: Married man dies after hotel sex with lover in China; woman fined Rs 7.5 lakh
item.description: A Chinese court has ordered a woman, Zhuang, to compensate the family of her deceased married lover, Zhou, with 62,000 Yuan. Zhou died of a heart attack after a hotel encounter. The court found Zhuang secondarily responsible for not seeking immediate help and for violating public order by having an affair, while the hotel was absolved of any fault.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Qatar Media Corporation and Al Jazeera Media Institute sign deal for joint training and media development
item.description: Qatar Media Corporation and Al Jazeera Media Institute have signed a strategic agreement to develop specialised media training programmes, enhance production capabilities, and build national media talent. The partnership includes practical training in Al Jazeera’s studios, expert workshops, and exclusive support for QMC staff, aiming to align Qatar’s media sector with international standards and future industry demands.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russia-Ukraine conflict: Moscow captures 2 villages in Donetsk region; advances towards Ukrainian logistics base
item.description: Russian forces have intensified their military campaign in Ukraine's Donetsk region, claiming the capture of Sredneye and Kleban-Byk. This advance brings Russian troops closer to Kostyantynivka, a strategically important town on the route to Kramatorsk. Kramatorsk serves as a vital logistics hub for Ukrainian forces, potentially disrupting supply lines if the advance continues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Racist Berlin street name to change after legal battle
item.description: Berlin's Mohrenstrasse, a street with a racist name rooted in Germany's colonial past, was slated to be renamed after Anton Wilhelm Amo, the first African-born scholar to earn a European doctorate. Despite years of lobbying and legal battles, residents initially blocked the change, but the courts ultimately upheld the renaming.

item.title: Oman’s hotel revenues rose 18% in the first six months of 2025, with tourist arrivals reaching 1.14 million
item.description: Oman's hospitality sector thrived in the first half of 2025, witnessing an 18% surge in hotel revenues alongside a 1.14 million increase in tourist arrivals. This growth is attributed to strategic tourism development, enhanced infrastructure, and effective marketing initiatives. The nation's Vision 2040 plan aims to further boost tourism, supported by substantial investments in new resorts and projects.
